No more curl processes. Good. Now let me use aria2c with multiple connections per file and 2 concurrent downloads.

aria2c is great because:
1. It supports multiple connections per file (e.g., 16 connections)
2. Each connection downloads a different part of the file
3. This effectively multiplies the throughput

Let me create an aria2 download script.

input.command:
cat > /tmp/download_14b_aria2.sh << 'SCRIPT'
#!/bin/bash
source /etc/network_turbo 2>/dev/null || true

BASE_URL="https://hf-mirror.com/Qwen/Qwen3-14B/resolve/main"
DEST="/dev/shm/Qwen3-14B"
mkdir -p "$DEST"

# Generate URL list for aria2
URLFILE="/tmp/aria2_urls.txt"
> "$URLFILE"

for i in $(seq 1 8); do
    SHARD=$(printf "model-%05d-of-00008.safetensors" $i)
    if [ ! -f "$DEST/$SHARD" ]; then
        echo "${BASE_URL}/${SHARD}" >> "$URLFILE"
        echo "  dir=$DEST" >> "$URLFILE"
        echo "  out=$SHARD" >> "$URLFILE"
    fi
done

echo "Downloading $(wc -l < $URLFILE | tr -d ' ') URL entries..."
# aria2c: 16 connections per file, 2 concurrent downloads, auto-retry
aria2c \
    --input-file="$URLFILE" \
    --split=16 \
    --max-connection-per-server=16 \
    --min-split-size=20M \
    --max-concurrent-downloads=2 \
    --max-tries=10 \
    --retry-wait=5 \
    --timeout=60 \
    --connect-timeout=30 \
    --continue=true \
    --file-allocation=none \
    --auto-file-renaming=false \
    --allow-overwrite=true \
    --console-log-level=notice \
    --summary-interval=30

echo "aria2c exit code: $?"
echo "ALL DOWNLOADS COMPLETE at $(date)"
du -sh "$DEST"
ls -lh "$DEST"/*.safetensors 2>/dev/null
SCRIPT
chmod +x /tmp/download_14b_aria2.sh
nohup bash /tmp/download_14b_aria2.sh > /tmp/download_14b_aria2.log 2>&1 &
echo $!
sleep 25 && tail -20 /tmp/download_14b_aria2.log 2>/dev/null; du -sh /dev/shm/Qwen3-14B/ 2>/dev/null; ps -p 198107 -o pid= 2>/dev/null && echo "RUNNING" || echo "DONE"
